Sports.title: Lionel Messi plays first game for Inter Miami since father's death... after devastated star hinted he could QUIT soccer in emotional tribute
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi played his first game for Inter Miami since the death of his father on Wednesday night.

The soccer star's father Jorge died at 68 on August 7 following a battle with illness that overshadowed the Argentina captain's mesmerizing World Cup campaign in the United States, in which he led his team to the final.

The devastated forward came onto the pitch in the 46th minute of Inter Miami's clash with Club Leon in the Leagues Cup tournament pitting MLS and Liga MX sides against each other.

Messi received a standing ovation from the audience at the Nu Stadium as he entered at halftime. His substitution had a positive impact on the side, but The Herons fell 3-2 to Leon.

The result officially eliminated Inter Miami from the knockout stages of the tournament, following their win over Atletico San Luis and a prior loss to CF Monterrey. Inter Miami reached the final of last year's tournament and won the 2023 edition of the Leagues Cup.

For Messi, the match was his first since the death of his father. It also came on the same day the Argentine posted a heartbreaking tribute on his Instagram account.

Lionel Messi made his return to Inter Miami days after the death of his father

Lionel's father, Jorge Messi, passed away on August 7 following a long battle with illness

Messi was a second-half substitute, but couldn't help Miami overcome a 3-2 loss to Club Leon

'Dad, I still can't believe you're gone,' the tribute read in Spanish. 'It hasn't sunk in yet, or rather, I don't want to accept it. It's very difficult for me to imagine never seeing you again, never talking to you again.

'I know you were suffering and that this is for the best, but you left too soon. We still had so much to enjoy together.

'I don't know what I'll do without you, I don't know how to go on. I only played football and now I have serious doubts that I'll continue doing that for much longer.

'You were by my side from the beginning, it was so close to the end. Why couldn't you hold on that little bit longer and we could have finished together?'

Longtime sporting rival Cristiano Ronaldo replied to the post, saying: 'A huge hug to you and yours in these tough times, Leo. Much strength.'

The Portuguese legend knows of Messi's heartache only too well after losing his father, Jose Dinis Aveiro, in 2005 to an alcoholism-related liver condition when he was aged just 20.

'I really don’t know my father 100 per cent,' Ronaldo told Piers Morgan in 2019. 'He was a drunk person. I never spoke with him, like a normal conversation. It was hard.'

Messi revealed that his father was the driving force behind his decision to play at this summer's World Cup, but his ageing legs prevented him from bringing the trophy home – with Spain winning 1-0 in the New York final.

Lionel Messi has thanked fans for their support following the death of his father Jorge (left)

Messi's father and agent died in Rosario, Argentina on Friday August 7

Jorge's death saw an outpouring of emotional tributes from the football world, including from Messi's first team Newell's Old Boys, as well as Barcelona and Argentina.

'You kept asking me to play in the last World Cup, and just a few days before it started, you got worse,' Messi's tribute continued. 'It was the first time you wouldn't be in a tournament, but Mom kept telling me you'd get better and be well enough to travel. I told you we were going to reach the final so you could travel.

'Every time a game ended, I waited and missed your message. That's when I realized the situation was really serious. Even so, I couldn't stop thinking about going as far as possible, to give you time and for you to see a game. We reached the final and you couldn't be there. I wanted to win it to bring it to you and show you a new one. I couldn't, my legs couldn't take it anymore. This time I tried to go against my physical limitations, but I couldn't. I never managed to feel well.

'When I arrived, you thought we'd lost the final on penalties. We couldn't talk about anything that happened. You couldn't enjoy any of it. We didn't win the championship, but you don't know how much we enjoyed every game. Once again, you were right: I had to be there and play.

'I'm telling you this because it was the only thing we couldn't talk about, because you already know everything else. We used to talk every day and see each other whenever possible, given my commitments.'

Messi missed Inter Miami's defeat by Monterrey on Sunday to return home in the wake of his father's passing, and thanked fans for their well wishes.

He added on his Instagram stories: 'I want to sincerely thank everyone for all the love, respect and enormous consideration you have shown me and my family during this incredibly painful time following the loss of my dad.

'Thank you for being there for us, for every message, every gesture and, above all, for respecting our grief and our privacy.'

Lionel Messi's father Jorge, pictured at the 2022 World Cup final, died at the age of 68

MESSI STATEMENT IN FULL 'Dad, I still can't believe you're gone. It hasn't sunk in yet, or rather, I don't want to accept it. It's very difficult for me to imagine never seeing you again, never talking to you again. I know you were suffering and that this is for the best, but you left too soon. We still had so much to enjoy together.' You kept asking me to play in the last World Cup, and just a few days before it started, you got worse. It was the first time you wouldn't be in a tournament, but Mom kept telling me you'd get better and be well enough to travel. I told you we were going to reach the final so you could travel. Every time a game ended, I waited and missed your message. That's when I realized the situation was really serious. Even so, I couldn't stop thinking about going as far as possible, to give you time and for you to see a game. We reached the final and you couldn't be there. I wanted to win it to bring it to you and show you a new one. I couldn't, my legs couldn't take it anymore. This time I tried to go against my physical limitations, but I couldn't. I never managed to feel well. When I arrived, you thought we'd lost the final on penalties. We couldn't talk about anything that happened. You couldn't enjoy any of it. We didn't win the championship, but you don't know how much we enjoyed every game. Once again, you were right: I had to be there and play. I'm telling you this because it was the only thing we couldn't talk about, because you already know everything else. We used to talk every day and see each other whenever possible, given my commitments. I don't know what I'll do without you, I don't know how to go on. I only played football and now I have serious doubts that I'll continue doing that for much longer. You were by my side from the beginning, it was so close to the end. Why couldn't you hold on that little bit longer and we could have finished together? I know that his happiness was seeing his family well, his wife, his children and, above all, without others knowing, seeing me play. It's always been like this since I was little. You'd take me to all the practices as soon as you got home from work. Many times, Mom would take me because you were working. Obviously, you never missed a game. How you suffered watching me, and how you enjoyed it, even though you never gave me many compliments. You were a father, a friend, and a businessman. You were always the person you needed to be in every situation and you never made a mistake. Aside from a few demands or arguments, you were always right. In the end, things always turned out exactly as you said. I will miss you very much, but you will always be present, especially in the upbringing of my children, because I teach and educate them as you did with me. Rest in peace and watch over us from up there as you did here. Thank you for everything. I love you, Dad.

Messi also posted a picture with his father, captioned: 'I love you, pa' in Spanish.

Football legend Messi was extremely close to his father, who also operated as his agent and de facto business manager throughout his career, overseeing his son's multi-million dollar empire off the pitch.

In recent months, though, the patriarch of the family had been dealing with an as-yet-unconfirmed medical issue that had seen him taken to hospital in his home country.

His illness first came to light when Lionel, 39, cried on the pitch at the World Cup in a rare public display of emotion.

After scoring a hat-trick against Algeria in Argentina's opening group game in Kansas City, Messi was questioned by journalists and said: 'No, honestly it's something completely unrelated to sports. It's been a few difficult days, complicated.'

Just hours later, journalist Eduardo Feinmann explained the reason for the tears in an interview on Radio Mitre, one of the country's most listened-to stations.

'This has to do with his father. His father is not in good health,' he said. 'For quite some time now, several months, since last year.

'And this week there were some situations that slightly worsened his health, and Messi is going through this internal struggle. In other words, like any human being.'

Messi stands in front of his family (including father Jorge (third left) in Rosario in October 2003

It has since been reported that Jorge suffered a 'medical episode' at his home in January of this year, and he was hospitalised as a result.

In the aftermath, he was said to have undergone cardiovascular and neurological tests, but no official diagnosis was shared by the family, who sought to keep Jorge's health out of the media.

Jorge's health became headline news again in June, when a broadcaster in Argentina falsely claimed he had died – before later issuing an emotional apology and stepping down from her job.

Lionel is the third of four children of Jorge and his wife Celia Cuccittini, and the pair remained together until his death.

They married in 1978 and split their time between Rosario and Miami, where their footballing superstar son currently plays for David Beckham's Inter Miami in Major League Soccer (MLS).

Before becoming Lionel's agent, Jorge worked for a steel manufacturer in Villa Constitucion, meeting his wife as a young man in Rosario – where the family then grew up.

Jorge arrives at son Lionel's wedding in 2017 with his wife Celia (L) and daughter Maria (R)

Messi has two older brothers, Rodrigo and Matias, and a younger sister, Maria Sol.

Jorge has been at Messi's side throughout his historic career, which began in Argentina with Newell's Old Boys, before he moved to Spain to join Barcelona's famed La Masia academy in 2000.

He became the greatest of all-time in an incredible 21 years in Barcelona, before stunning the world with a move to Paris Saint-Germain – orchestrated by Jorge – in 2021.

After two seasons in the French capital, he moved to MLS and Inter Miami, where he remains to this day at the age of 39.

While Lionel's career has been magical on the pitch, it has not been without controversy off it, with Jorge famously by his son's side throughout his tax fraud case in 2016.

The pair sat together in front of the court, with Jorge in his role as his son's business manager, with the prosecution alleging that Messi failed to properly pay tax on income from his image rights between 2007 and 2009.

Ultimately, both father and son were convicted of three tax offenses, initially each receiving suspended 21-month prison sentences.

Jorge's sentence was subsequently reduced to 15 months upon review in 2017 by Spain's Supreme Court, with the pair also hit with substantial fines.

Sports.title: EFL 2026-27 predictions with Championship winners decided as West Ham and Wolves discover fate
Sports.content:
Forgive me for going full Jamie O'Hara here, but it's time to rejoice: proper football is BACK.

Yes, last week's Carabao Cup games - and the World Cup - were a nice little distraction to tide us over but the real stuff is back this weekend. And there's plenty of talking points to get stuck into before we prepare to embark on the white-knuckle ride that is a 46 game EFL season.

In the Championship, it's the land of the fallen giants with West Ham, Wolves and Burnley dropping back into the second tier. Will they make an instant return? Or can the teams who narrowly missed out on promotion last year, such as Middlesbrough, Millwall and Southampton, beat them to the post? Don't forget, the top eight will make up the play-offs this year.

Then in League One, Leicester City are the big scalp after dropping into arguably the most unpredictable division of all. They will vie with Sheffield Wednesday and Jack Wilshere's Luton Town for promotion. And in League Two, can Gary Neville and David Beckham's Salford City finally get over the line after some eye-catching transfer business?

‌



Nobody really knows. But Mirror Football's crack team have taken a stab at predicting the big winners and losers...

James Whaling

Championship winners: West Ham

Promoted: Middlesbrough, Wolves

‌



Relegated: Lincoln, Charlton, Blackburn

Top scorer: Raul Jimenez

Surprise package: Portsmouth

League One winners: Leicester

‌



League Two winners: Salford

It's hard to see West Ham not making an immediate return to the top flight. Keeping hold of Jarrod Bowen is an unbelievable bit of business and their squad should be far too strong for the second tier. Middlesbrough look ready to join them in the Premier League after another near-miss last term, somehow managing to lose twice in the playoffs. I fancy Wolves to also bounce straight back, fired by the goals of the returning Raul Jimenez.

At the wrong end of the league, I think Blackburn may sail too close to the sun one too many times and slip into the third division. Charlton look set for another season of struggle and, as well as Lincoln have done reaching the Championship, I think they may find it difficult.

Portsmouth have made some shrewd additions in the transfer window and will be strong at home. Manager John Mousinho has another season of Championship experience under his belt and I think they may surprise a few.

‌



Leicester, similarly to West Ham, have a squad far too strong for the level they are playing at and should bounce straight back to the Championship. Gary Neville, David Beckham and Salford City to win League Two.

View 6 Images Jarrod Bowen and West Ham are the red-hot favourites to win the Championship (Image: Rob Newell/CameraSport)

Ben Husband

Championship winners: Wolves

Promoted: West Ham, Middlesbrough

‌



Relegated: Bolton, Lincoln, Blackburn

Top scorer: Raul Jimenez

Surprise package: QPR

League One winners: Leicester

‌



League Two winners: Salford

I know what you’re thinking…way to go out on a limb. The Championship prediction is made with more than a hint of bias, but I do think if Wolves can get one or two more faces through the door before the window closes they could be formidable. Simply put, a squad including Andre, Kieran Trippier, Raul Jimenez, Mateus Mane and Adam Armstrong should be enough to get it done. Even with some fierce competition from the likes of West Ham, Middlesbrough and Southampton - who will miss out due to their points deduction.

In League One, despite how disastrous his Rangers reign was, Russell Martin is a more than good enough manager to get Leicester back into the Championship. Although they will need to start well to arrest the slide that is now two years in the making.

And in League Two, the arrivals of Macauley Langstaff and Luke Molyneux - to a side that made the play-off final last season - should be enough for Salford City.

‌



Dan Marsh

Championship winners: Wolves

Promoted: Middlesbrough, Norwich

Relegated: Bolton, Charlton, Lincoln

Top scorer: Will Lankshear

‌



Surprise package: Cardiff City

League One winners: Luton Town

League Two winners: Bristol Rovers

Everyone is having West Ham as the bankers to win the league but I'm not convinced Nuno Espirito Santo's pragmatic approach necessarily translates into a top two finish. Their squad is a joke, though, while and they'll be amongst the top teams, clubs will relish the prospect of going to the London Stadium and claiming a major scalp. The scrutiny on West Ham should open the door for Wolves to mount a title challenge with slightly less pressure. They have a manager who has no Championship experience but their squad, too, does not belong at this level and they are my picks for the title. Middlesbrough have levelled up in key areas, namely in goal (Radek Vitek over Sol Brynn) and up front, where Will Lankshear should feast if Boro can repeat the buffet of chances they produced for their forwards last season. I fancy them to finish second with Norwich, resurgent after appointing Philippe Clement midway through the season, a force in the play-offs.

‌



At the other end of the table, Bolton and Charlton have had underwhelming transfer windows. Bolton will be right up against it after coming up through the play-offs, while Charlton, who eventually got over the line last season after winning the previous year's play-offs, have not signed the creative players required for them to 'evolve' as Nathan Jones wishes. Lincoln City have momentum and the nucleus of the squad that destroyed League One last year but losing Michael Skubala and their best player, Jack Moylan, makes an already daunting task even more difficult. Cardiff City are my surprise package tip; I fancy Brian Barry-Murphy's expansive style will translate well to the Championship and star striker Yousef Salech will also handle the step up with aplomb.

Everybody is tipping Leicester to romp League One so I'll go against the curve and tip Luton; they finished the season strongly after winning the EFL Trophy and Jack Wilshere will be all the better for the experience. Salford City have done some eye-catching business and again are heavily fancied to win League Two but Steve Evans has rebuilt Bristol Rovers and I can see them being there or thereabouts under him.

View 6 Images Wolves are likely to be among the teams vying for promotion (Image: David Rogers)

Felix Keith

Championship winners: West Ham

‌



Promoted: Middlesbrough, Norwich City

Relegated: Portsmouth, Cardiff, QPR

Top scorer: Jarrod Bowen

Surprise package: Norwich City

‌



League One winners: Leicester City

League Two winners: Salford City

It really is hard to look past West Ham. Nuno Espirito Santo has been there and done it and, as many have pointed out, Bowen is far too good for the Championship. Something will have to go very wrong for the Hammers to mess it up. Southampton have (so far) managed to hold onto their best players, barring Shea Charles, so should be right in the mix for promotion again. But Tonda Eckert still has an FA charge hanging over his head, which could prompt a lengthy touchline ban. The fallout from Spygate could cost them and help Middlesbrough.

Norwich were a team transformed after Philippe Clement’s arrival last season. They’re only eighth favourites with the bookies for promotion but I can see them surprising a few.

‌



Portsmouth and QPR survived last season but were largely dreadful and could help Lincoln stay up after promotion from League One.

I fancy Russell Martin to get Leicester back up, despite losing some exciting players and the financial might behind the Salford project can’t afford it to stall much longer.

Samuel Meade

Championship winners: West HamPromoted: Middlesbrough, MillwallRelegated: Watford, Bolton, CardiffTop scorer: Jarrod BowenSurprise package: LincolnLeague One winners: LeicesterLeague Two winners: Port Vale The Hammers keeping hold of Nuno Espirito Santo and Jarrod Bowen is their two best bits of business and they'll have too much not to return immediately. Lincoln as a surprise may raise eyebrows, given they won League One with more than 100 points, but plenty have tipped them for the drop.

Leicester are an obvious contender for League One and I'm not convinced by Salford in League Two, despite them being promotion favourites.

‌



View 6 Images New boy Will Lankshear will spearhead Middlesbrough's bid for promotion (Image: Trevor Wilkinson/NurPhoto)

Jeremy Cross

Championship winners: Southampton

Promoted: West Ham, Middlesbrough

Relegated: Watford, Stoke, Charlton

‌



Top scorer: Jarrod Bowen

Surprise package: Millwall

League One winners: Leicester City

League Two winners: Bristol Rovers

‌



Southampton have a lot to prove to the game and themselves this season, following their shameful end to the last one. But getting caught spying on play-off opponents Middlesbrough will give the Saints more than enough fuel to come back fighting again, only this time legally, hopefully. Despite his dubious approach and the subsequent four point deduction, manager Tonda Eckert has done a fine job on the south coast. The season-long loan signing of striker Divin Mubama from Manchester City could prove to be a shrewd move, while the arrival of Lewis Dobbin from Aston Villa in a £10m deal will bring some class and composure to the team.

Middlesbrough have been promotion contenders for a few seasons now, and have only finished outside the top eight once since 2022, so this could well be their time to make a return to the top flight. West Ham, meanwhile, have kept hold of their two best assets despite relegation from the Premier League, in the shape of manager Nuno Santo and England international Jarrod Bowen. Bowen is too good for the Championship, and should be the best player in the entire league this season. If he can maintain the form he's capable of, his goals should give the Hammers an immediate return to the top flight.

Leicester still have the quality to get back into the Championship from League One, while Bristol Rovers look to be the best placed team to win League Two ahead of Salford City.

Brian Dick

Championship winners: West Ham United

‌



Promoted: Middlesbrough, Southampton

Relegated: Lincoln City, Bolton Wanderers, Blackburn Rovers

Top scorer: Jarrod Bowen

Surprise package: Norwich City

‌



League One winners: Leicester City

League Two winners: Barnet

West Ham are the most obvious Championship winners since Newcastle United came down a few years ago. In Nuno they have a proven manager who has won the league before, Jarrod Bowen who will be the best player in the division and a financial muscle and set-up that separates them from the field.

Middlesbrough were the best team in the league for so long last season but ran out of goals, a shortcoming they look to have addressed. Tonda Eckert may have landed in hot water but if he survives any sanction after Spygate, it was clear he had the Saints on the charge last term. Norwich also came like a train after the appointment of Philippe Clement and have recruited well.

‌



Leicester will be too strong not to bounce back from League One, as long as they keep their noses clean on the financial front. Barnet look well-placed to improve on last season’s eighth.

View 6 Images Russell Martin will lead Leicester City in League One (Image: Plumb Images/Leicester City FC)

Peter Smith

Championship winners: West Ham

Promoted: Southampton

‌



Relegated: Lincoln, Bolton, Portsmouth

Top scorer: Taty Castellanos

Surprise package: Stoke City

League One winners: Leicester City

‌



League Two winners: Salford City

The relegated three might have endured varying levels of chaos on their way back to the Championship but their squads should still be strong enough to set the pace. Then again, Southampton had the best squad last year and it took until they changed manager to show it. Even with a points deduction, a couple of key departures and the disdain of their rivals they will be around about it this time.

It is going to be so tight between most of the rest and it will come down to who has a knack of tipping close games in their favour. Stoke’s chances of a good year at last hang on an overhauled midfield. Most seasons since 2018 have all-but finished in January so, with the play-off expansion, it would be a dream for supporters to go into the spring feeling alive.

Leigh Curtis

Championship winners: West Ham

‌



Promoted: Wolves (second), Norwich (playoffs)

Relegated: Portsmouth, Blackburn, Bolton

Top scorer: Jarrod Bowen

Surprise package: Lincoln City

‌



League One winners: Leicester City

League Two winners: Salford City

West Ham's squad is just too good to be at this level for any longer than a season. Keeping Jarrod Bowen was huge and Nuno, despite relegation last season, is still a good and wily manager. I can't see beyond them for the title and I still expect them to strengthen in the transfer market too. It would be a huge shock if they didn't win it. Wolves have made a couple of impressive signings and I fully expect them to be challenging West Ham for the crown. César Peixoto is new to English football, but he looks to have them better organised from what I've seen in pre-season. Plus they aren't finished in the market. As for the playoffs, I was hugely impressed by Norwich last season towards the back end of the campaign. Had a good run under Phillipe Clement. I like the Andre Brooks signing and their forwards are a real handful. I'm predicting them to go up at Wembley. I love Tony Mowbray, but I think he's got his hands full at Blackburn in trying to keep them in the league this season. The signings haven't really caught the eye and there's still problems that need resolving. Portsmouth I thought would go down last year, but they had a decent run towards the back end of the campaign that got them out of trouble, but I think this might be the year. And Bolton I think could be in danger purely because the first season out of League One is always tough because the leap from that to the Championship is vast.

View 6 Images Former Millwall man Macaulay Langstaff will lead the line for League Two promotion hopefuls Salford City this season (Image: Harriet Massey)

‌



Lincoln may well surprise a few people this year. They have a unique way of playing, but they are well organised, their excellent at set-pieces and their pressing is very good. In Ben House they have an absolute machine who never stops running. Sincil Bank is not the easiest place to visit either.

Top scorer is a tough one to call but I am going to say Jarrod Bowen, although I think Mohamed Toure at Norwich and Adam Armstrong at Wolves will run him very close.

In League One, I just think Leicester will be too strong for the division really. Once they get acclimatised the division, they should bounce back straight back. Salford have had an excellent summer of recruitment in the division below and Macualey Langstaff will score bundles at that level. Unbelievable signing for the level.

Tom Coleman

Championship winners: West Ham

‌



Promoted: Wolves, Middlesbrough

Relegated: Lincoln, Charlton, Blackburn

Top scorer: Jarrod Bowen

Surprise package: Swansea City

‌



League One winners: Leicester City

League Two winners: Salford

West Ham have to be favourites to go back up to the Premier League as champions. They've got such a strong squad for this level and I strongly suspect Jarrod Bowen will tear up the division and score loads of goals. Last season's Golden Boot winner Zan Vipotnik will also hope to be in the mix. Middlesbrough really impressed me under Kim Hellberg and I suspect they'll be an even better prospect this time around. Wolves also look to be firmly in the hunt.

At the other end, I think Lincoln will find the step up just a bit too much, but I think Cardiff City and Bolton might just have enough for some reason. Charlton and Blackburn just about escaped last time out but I think they might just struggle this time around.

‌



As for the surprise package, I really like what Swansea have done this summer. They've strengthened in key areas and if they can keep hold of Vipotnik they'll have three top forwards for this level with Adam Idah and Ross Stewart also on the books. I wouldn't be at all surprised if they're part of the play-off conversation.

Nathan Ridley

Championship winners: Middlesbrough

Promoted: West Ham, WolvesRelegated: Lincoln, Charlton, PrestonTop scorer: Jarrod BowenSurprise package: NorwichLeague One winners: LeicesterLeague Two winners: Chesterfield

I can't see any spying from stopping Middlesbrough this year, with Kim Hellberg having made quality additions in key areas over the summer. I'm then backing West Ham to finish second with their stacked squad - hence my pick for top scorer, Jarrod Bowen - and Wolves to win the play-offs.

‌



Going down, I don't see Lincoln's managerial setup working while I think Charlton and Preston's boardroom uncertainty will permeate onto the pitch. Norwich, meanwhile, are almost in danger of the dark horse curse given the amount of fans and pundits tipping them for a play-off finish.

In League One, I can't look past Leicester. And I'll go with Chesterfield for the League Two title - it genuinely would've been York had they not sacked Stuart Maynard.

Sports.title: PSG chief drops transfer bombshell on Liverpool target Bradley Barcola
Sports.content:
PSG chief drops transfer bombshell on Liverpool target Bradley Barcola

Liverpool are still keen to sign Bradley Barcola and although Paris Saint-Germain's price tag is causing an issue, the French giants are officially open to selling him

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola is top of Liverpool's shopping list (Image: FRANCK FIFE/AFP via Getty Images)

Paris Saint-Germain chairman Nasser Al-Khelaifi has refused to rule out selling Bradley Barcola in a boost to Liverpool's chances of signing him. Barcola, 23, remains the Reds' top target in the final knockings of the summer transfer window.

But negotiations have been at an impasse as PSG look to bank the maximum fee for the winger, who they value at an eye-watering £145million amid from Arsenal, too. Barcola was an unused substitute as Luis Enrique's side beat Aston Villa 2-1 to win the UEFA Super Cup in Salzburg on Wednesday, having only returned to training following the World Cup earlier this week.

Post-match, Al-Khelaifi was asked about the France international's future and couldn't give a definitive answer. "We're working calmly, we don't talk too much," Al-Khelaifi told Canal Plus.

"I can't say whether he will leave or not ... Today, he is a PSG player. We'll see."

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

The chairman's comments came after Enrique kept tight-lipped before the match. "I don't know and I don't want to speak about any player individually," the PSG boss stated.

"Because it's always dangerous when you are asking something positive or negative about a player. I stay focused on my team."

While the victory saw Barcola collect a fourth European medal in just over three years at PSG, the goals were scored by two players ahead of him in the pecking order. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia gave the Champions League holders an early lead before Villa equalised prior to half-time through Brian Madjo's strike. Desire Doue then restored PSG's advantage in the second half.

How much should Liverpool pay for Bradley Barcola? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola didn't feature against Aston Villa (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images)

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola also hasn't spoken about Barcola, although he his desire to sign a wide forward is no secret. "We definitely need to sign a winger," Iraola stated last month.

"But there are other situations where we will have to analyse what the market gives you, what is the cost, how we also see the players we have We have some tricky positions where we have injured players that we trust, but it is still not the ideal situation, so it will depend on a lot of things."

Sports.title: A-level results day: Premier League stars and their achievements before making millions
Sports.content:
A-level results day: Premier League stars and their achievements before making millions

A-Level results have been released and many Premier League stars also pursued higher education alongside their footballing careers

View 3 Images Andrey Arshavin pursued a degree before his Arsenal heyday (Image: Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

Several Premier League stars have excelled in the classroom as well as on the football pitch. Thousands of students will learn their A-level results on Thursday and many top footballers understand the importance of education.

‌



While few top-flight stars take A-level exams, choosing to prioritise making their way up the academy ladder, a handful of footballers are known for their academic achievements. Arsenal’s Bukayo Saka got four A*s and three As in his GCSEs, Manchester United defender Harry Maguire earned similar results, while Chelsea legend Frank Lampard ’s 11 GCSEs included an A* in Latin.

‌



As students discover their A-Level results and decide on their next steps, several footballers have previously opted to study for degrees, either alongside or after their playing career. “These are super-clever individuals in terms of how their brain works,” Predrag Petrovic of the Karolinska Institute, who studied footballers’ cognitive abilities, told The Times in 2025.

‌



“Maybe some of them are not as schooled but you absolutely cannot dismiss their brains.” Here is a look at the Premier League stars who also pursued higher education.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Andrey Arshavin

Arsenal icon Andrey Arshavin enrolled in the St Petersburg State University of Technology and Design as a 17-year-old. He later switched to a fashion design degree due to the demands of his budding football career and later developed his own clothing line.

‌



Forgotten ex-Man Utd star reveals Bruno Fernandes gesture that shows his true colours READ MORE :

Carabao Cup fixture chaos as Chelsea embroiled in crazy eight-game domino effect READ MORE :

"I enrolled in the chemical technology department,” Arshavin recalled. "But when I began training with Zenit I had to miss a lot of classes. I transferred to the clothes design department. I have designed several garments myself."

Duncan Watmore

Former Sunderland player Duncan Watmore, 32, began his footballing career with non-league Altrincham before earning a Premier League move to the Black Cats in 2013. Despite becoming a top-flight star, Watmore was unwilling to stop his education.

The forward had been studying economics and business management at the University of Manchester and transferred to Newcastle University upon joining Sunderland. The 32-year-old, who recently hung up his boots, graduated with a first-class honours degree in January 2015.

‌



View 3 Images Former Belgium teammates Simon Mingolet and Romelu Lukaku have both earned qualifications (Image: Angelo Blankespoor/Soccrates/Getty Images)

Romelu Lukaku

Romelu Lukaku has enjoyed a glittering career that has seen him lead the line for the likes of Manchester United, Chelsea and Inter Milan. The 33-year-old is also Belgium’s record scorer with 93 goals.

However, the striker has also been committed to his studies as he reportedly holds a degree in public relations and tourism. Meanwhile, Lukaku can speak eight languages: English, Spanish, Portuguese, Dutch, French, German, Italian and Lingala.

‌



Simon Mingolet

Former Liverpool and Sunderland goalkeeper Simon Mingolet has several career options after recently hanging up his gloves. The 38-year-old holds a degree in political science and already owns a coffee shop in his native Belgium.

View 3 Images Juan Mata has earned two degrees (Image: Steve Christo - Corbis/Corbis via Getty Images)

Juan Mata

Juan Mata starred for Manchester United and Chelsea in the Premier League, winning two FA Cups and the Champions League during his time in England. The intelligent Spanish midfielder also focused on his education, earning degrees in marketing and sports science.

Clarke Carlisle

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Andoni Iraola set to be handed new transfer priority as double update emerges
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Andoni Iraola set to be handed new transfer priority as double update emerges

Liverpool's stuttering summer transfer window could about to become even more complicated

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola is looking to add to his squad this summer (Image: 2026 Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA)

Liverpool could be facing another transfer headache this summer. The window slams shut on September 1 and the Reds are still scrambling to get a mega-money deal over the line for PSG winger Bradley Barcola.

‌



Andoni Iraola's priority has been bolstering Liverpool's attack, namely securing a replacement for Mohamed Salah, and supplementing their forward line as a whole. However, the Reds are now braced for interest in two of their own midfielders.

‌



The updates mean Liverpool's Basque head coach may now have to pivot his attentions to strengthening his engine room. This would no doubt be a monumental task given that the Reds' hierarchy are still focusing their energies on the last third of the pitch.

‌



Alexis Mac Allister interest

Liverpool are braced for interest in Alexis Mac Allister this summer. Galatasaray have lodged their interest in recruiting the 27-year-old, according to reports in Turkey.

That interest has so far been declared via intermediaries to determine a price and the Argentine's wage demands, according to Yeni Asir. However, that's not all.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



According to talkSPORT, Manchester City have also shortlisted the World Cup-winner as they look to replace Rodri, who could be on his way to Barcelona this summer. However, the report stresses that there's been "no contact or developments" on any deal to take the midfielder to Manchester.

Mac Allister has been a regular in the Reds' midfield since his arrival from Brighton in 2023. However, he has now entered the final two years of his Anfield contract and suffered a dip in form last season, which saw him touted for an exit this summer.

View 3 Images Alexis Mac Allister (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

‌



Should he leave, Iraola would have to refocus his energies on replacing the star, with the Reds currently relying on Mac Allister, Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai as three of his senior midfielders. Harvey Elliott, Trey Nyoni, Wataru Endo and Stefan Bajcetic are also options, but all except Nyoni have also been linked with an exit this summer.

Sky Italia are also reporting that Curtis Jones is close to joining Inter Milan. Inter have moved closer to offloading midfielder Davide Frattesi to Lazio on loan, with the Rome club reportedly having reached a verbal agreement with the player, according to Fabrizio Romano.

‌



The journalist says an £850,000 loan fee, with a £11m option to buy, is in place, before formal steps are to follow. Once that deal is done, it's believed Inter will press ahead with a move for Jones.

View 3 Images Inter Milan are interested in signing Curtis Jones (Image: Liverpool FC, Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Inter have registered a strong interest in the midfielder and are willing to pay £30m for the 25-year-old, who is in the final year of his contract at Anfield. It's believed the Reds are looking for around £35m for the player.

Sports.title: PSG continue to dominate Europe as Aston Villa narrowly beaten in UEFA Super Cup
Sports.content:
PSG continue to dominate Europe as Aston Villa narrowly beaten in UEFA Super Cup

PARIS SAINT-GERMAIN 2-1 ASTON VILLA: The season curtain-raiser between the Champions League holders and the UEFA Cup victors was narrowly won by Luis Enrique's side

View 2 Images Desire Doue scored the goal that won PSG the UEFA Super Cup (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista)

Paris Saint-Germain reaffirmed their status as the kings of Europe by beating their former boss, Unai Emery, and Aston Villa 2-1 to win the UEFA Super Cup in Austria.

‌



The UEFA Cup holders lined up below full strength with Emi Martinez, Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins all missing following the World Cup. But even at full strength, Villa would have been up against it playing the team who destroyed some of Europe's elite on their way to winning a second successive Champions League title last season.

‌



Khvicha Kvaratskhelia broke the deadlock in style for the French giants 20 minutes in, chopping back onto his right foot on the left-hand side of the penalty area and whipping a ferocious effort past the helpless Marco Bizot. The goal was the Georgian winger's reward for an electric start to proceedings and left Villa with a mountain to climb.

‌



As impressive as PSG looked going forward, it was not all one way traffic; Villa's young guns up front, Brian Madjo and George Hemmings were in the thick of the action with Madjo going close twice in the team's pursuit of an equaliser.

View 2 Images Brian Madjo scored for Aston Villa before half-time to level proceedings (Image: Aston Villa FC)

The 17-year-old forward finally got the goal his endeavour deserved on the stroke of half-time when he was picked out by John McGinn. Madjo lashed the ball into the roof of the net, sparking jubilant scenes.

‌



Both teams had chances to nudge ahead as an entertaining second half wore on.

But it was Desire Doue who struck on the hour mark to break Aston Villa hearts, with the goal initially being chalked off for offside. Replays showed the Frenchman was well on, though, as PSG celebrated once more.

Villa continued to push for an equaliser and went agonisingly close when Alysson, a second half substitute, fired a low ball across the penalty area which evaded both Tammy Abraham and Ian Maatsen after good work from the former.

Article continues below

Ousmane Dembele almost added a third for PSG before Emi Buendia spurned a golden chance to equalise in the dying embers of added time, heading a dangerous cross wide.

Sports.title: Man Utd vs Leeds United friendly finishes early as multiple pitch invaders stop match
Sports.content:
Man Utd vs Leeds United friendly finishes early as multiple pitch invaders stop match

Manchester United's pre-season clash with Leeds United was brought to a premature close

View 2 Images A fan runs on the pitch which interrupts Manchester United's friendly with Leeds United. (Image: PA Wire)

Manchester United's game against Leeds United was brought to a premature halt as pitch invaders raced onto the pitch for selfies with some of the big-name stars. As the ball went out of play in the 89th minute following a Manchester United attack, five or six children raced onto the pitch to pose for pictures with some of their favourite players.

‌



Two made their way to the middle of the pitch for a picture with Youri Tielemans, who stopped what he was doing to pose for the young lads. The two kids then ran off the field of play, one with his hands aloft as he was cheered by the crowd, while a member of the security team gestured for them to leave the pitch.

‌



The security appeared to be booed by those in the ground, before cheers broke out as they safely made their way back into the stands. Their success prompted more kids to run onto the pitch, this time one United fan made a beeline for Bruno Fernandes, who also entertained the youngster, posing for a picture as more cheers broke out.

‌



Man Utd frustrated by Leeds as Bruno Fernandes reminder sent - 5 talking points READ MORE :

More members of the security team made their way onto the pitch to remove the children, who had delayed play by two minutes, and referee Neil Doyle blew the whistle early to end the game.

Speaking on ITV commentary, Sam Matterface said: "Some young supporters have come running onto the pitch, which is not particularly helpful but they're being entertained by some of the senior players.

‌



"I don't think Daniel Farke is too happy about it. One has become two, now two has become three. They're all kids who are going up for selfies which is not great.

"Because the players are standing there and doing it, it's encouraging more to come on and do it. We've got a fourth one coming on which has caused a delay to proceedings and it makes a mockery of the security.

"A fifth one escapes a barrier and starts charging on, oh and a sixth. We'll have the whole lot on in a minute. Oh dear. It's a little bit of fun but it's not the greatest end to the match itself and the referee has decided to call a halt to proceedings to finish the game off and it'll be a penalty shootout at the end of the match.

‌



"Those incursions onto the pitch by some of the younger fans has just brought us to a premature close. We will have a penalty shootout for you very shortly."

View 2 Images A fan runs onto the pitch as he attempts to take a selfie with Manchester United's Youri Tielemans during the friendly with Leeds. (Image: PA Wire)

Joshua Zirkzee had given United the lead infront of a packed out Croke Park in the 16th minute after some great play from Bryan Mbeumo down the left.

‌



However, their lead lasted just 13 minutes with Brenden Aaronson equalising just before the half hour mark. Neither side was able to find a breakthrough and a penalty shootout was needed to separate the two teams.

The PA announcer had to interrupt the shootout to warn fans not to invade the pitch during the shootout as play would have to stop once more.

United ran out 5-4 winners with Harry Wilson and James Justin missing from the spot, with Fernandes missing for Carrick's side.

Sports.title: Bruno Guimaraes' position decided as Myles Lewis-Skelly sends Arsenal message - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimaraes' position decided as Myles Lewis-Skelly sends Arsenal message - 5 talking points

Arsenal took on Como at the Emirates Stadium in their final pre-season match before the Community Shield vs Man City

View 4 Images Myles Lewis-Skelly scored amid talk of him leaving Arsenal this summer

Arsenal have concluded their pre-season campaign, with eyes now on the weekend's Community Shield against Manchester City - the two teams meet in Cardiff on Sunday.

‌



In the final game before that meeting, the Gunners took on Italian side Como at the Emirates Stadium, a match which saw Cesc Fabregas return to his former home. The game ended in a 1-1 draw, with Arsenal winning thanks to a penalty shootout.

‌



Arsenal took the lead just after the first-half drinks break. Myles Lewis-Skelly capitalised on a mistake from Como goalkeeper Jean Butez. His clearance eventually found its way to Gabriel Martinelli, who got the ball back to the midfielder and he made no mistake to put Arsenal 1-0 up.

‌



But the Gunners didn't go into half time leading with Como making the most of a counter-attack. The ball made its way to Martin Baturina, who cut in from the left and gave Kepa Arrizabalaga no chance with a great finish to make it 1-1.

Arsenal reignite Ezri Konsa transfer hopes but face massive Aston Villa problem READ MORE :

Arsenal set to finally break record for transfer sale as bid submitted for Gabriel Martinelli READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

That's how the score would remain, despite chances for both sides. That meant that penalties were needed to separate the two sides, with summer signing Christos Tzolis scoring the decisive spot kick.

‌



Mirror Football has taken a look at some of the biggest talking points from the game.

Myles Lewis-Skelly message

Like previous pre-season games, Lewis-Skelly was named in the starting XI, despite being linked with a move away from the Emirates in recent days.

The 19-year-old played in midfield just in front of the back four. He also got forward when given the chance, and was rewarded by scoring the opening goal.

‌



He capitalised on a mistake from the Como goalkeeper, to put Arsenal 1-0 up just after the first-half drinks break. His celebration saw him make a heart with his hands, which was a clear sign of where his head is at. He received a warm reception from the Emirates crowd when he was replaced in the second half.

Bruno Guimaraes role

Bruno Guimaraes completed a £75 million move to Arsenal from Newcastle United last week. The Brazilian came on at half-time to make his debut for the club, much to the delight of those at the Emirates. He played a similar role to Declan Rice, playing just in front of Lewis-Skelly.

View 4 Images Bruno Guimaraes made his Arsenal debut vs Como (Image: John Walton/PA Wire)

‌



As expected, Guimaraes was always eager to get on the ball and make something happen. He also got back well and helped prevent a counter-attack, leading to chants of 'Bruno' from the home crowd. His introduction did allow Lewis-Skelly to get forward a bit more often.

Defensive issues

Despite not giving up many chances in the first-half, Arteta would have been frustrated to concede one of the few that Como had. While it was a great finish, there may have been an argument that more could have done to stop the ball getting to that position in the first place.

Defensive concerns are something that has dominated pre-season, with the team having conceded three goals in each of their previous two games against Real Betis and Borussia Dortmund. It's something that Arsenal will want to tighten up going into Sunday's Community Shield.

‌



If Arsenal give Man City similar chances, then they are likely to take them. Even if the game is seen as a 'glorified friendly', losing to title rivals ahead of the start of the season is not the ideal preparation for their Premier League opener.

Mikel Arteta decision

Marli Salmon was again given a chance to impress for Arsenal as he was named alongside Gabriel Magalhaes at the heart of defence. The injury to William Saliba has left Arteta short in the area.

View 4 Images Cesc Fabregas was back at the Emirates

‌



They have been linked with Aston Villa defender Ezri Konsa, but it seems the two teams are still far apart in their valuation. Salmon could provide a solution if Arsenal are unable to bring in a new defender in the transfer window, having impressed again against Como.

Despite being just 16, he earned praise for his composure, strength and willingness to step out of defence with the ball when needed.

Either way, a decision will have to be made over his short-term future. But it will be a bit of a waiting game for Arsenal.

‌



Players have to be on a professional contract to go out on loan, and they can't sign that contract until they are 17 years old. Salmon doesn't turn 17 until August 29, meaning that there will be just a few days for Arsenal to sort out a loan deal if they decide to send him out for valuable game time.

View 4 Images Marli Salmon staked his case for more involvement

It will be less complicated for Theo Julienne, who made his first pre-season appearance by starting at left-back. The 18-year-old didn’t look out of place, but a loan deal and regular game time this season may benefit him.

‌



Ethan Nwaneri chance

Ethan Nwaneri is another player who may have been playing for a place in the starting XI for the season opener against Coventry City in under two weeks.

Competition for places means that in the number 10 role Nwaneri has Max Dowman, Eberechi Eze and Martin Odegaard vying for the same spot.

Article continues below

With Declan Rice still not back after the World Cup, Nwaneri was given the chance to impress in a slightly deeper role. Lewis-Skelly sitting allowed him to go forward and help Eze in the number 10 role; there was then more of an interchange when Fabio Vieira was introduced after half an hour.

He caught the eye in the opening stages, often playing a big role in the high press, which led to some early chances. He did, however, fade as the half went on and was replaced by Guimaraes at halftime.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
