Jharkhand protest enters 20th day

NEW DELHI: Student leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who is on an indefinite hunger strike over alleged irregularities in Jharkhand recruitment examinations, remains hospitalised at Sadar Hospital in Ranchi, with protesting students alleging that the state government is withholding information about his health to weaken their agitation.Meanwhile, former Jharkhand chief minister Raghubar Das on Thursday visited Mahto at the hospital and enquired about his health.Mahto has been on hunger strike for 11 days and is undergoing treatment after he was injured during a police lathi-charge on August 10. The wider protest by JPSC and JSSC aspirants entered its 20th day on Thursday, with students continuing their agitation at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium.The protesting students have alleged that the government is not allowing them to meet Mahto at the hospital and is withholding details about his health.Mahto was moved to Sadar Hospital by the administration late Monday evening after police used force to disperse thousands of aspirants who had marched towards the state assembly.In a post on X, Mahto said: "Former Chief Minister of Jharkhand Raghubar Das ji reached the hospital and inquired about my well-being, while also assuring support for our movement."Das had on Wednesday threatened to go on a hunger strike if the demand for a CBI probe was not fulfilled within a week.He has also sought compensation of Rs 1 crore each for the families of 19 people who died during the 2024 excise constable physical examination.The BJP has accused the Hemant Soren government of suppressing the student movement, while the Congress has accused the saffron party of politicising the agitation and alleged that it brought workers from outside Jharkhand to disrupt the protests.On Tuesday, in a message shared on social media, Mahto said "My body is undergoing treatment in the hospital bed, but my soul and resolve are at the Satyagraha site where students and youth are engaged in a just struggle for their future. The indefinite hunger strike continues on its 11th day in Sadar Hospital."Mahto has also sought permission from the hospital authorities to return to the protest site. In a handwritten application to the Civil Surgeon, he said being separated from the protesting students was causing him greater distress than his physical ailments.He cited his responsibility towards thousands of students protesting against alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations and sought permission to rejoin them.The protesters have been demanding cancellation of the JSSC-CGL examination, a CBI probe into alleged irregularities and reforms in the recruitment process. They have alleged that their demands have not been fully accepted by the state government.The studentsâ agitation over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations entered its 20th day on Thursday. The JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch has been demonstrating at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, demanding greater transparency in recruitment examinations, cancellation of several tests and an independent probe by the CBI or a panel of retired judges from outside Jharkhand.Tensions escalated on Monday when JPSC and JSSC aspirants marched towards the state assembly. Police used batons, water cannons and tear gas to disperse the protesters.Mahto was among those taken to hospital after the confrontation. He later sought permission to leave the hospital and return to the protest site, saying his presence with the students was important to the movement.The ABVP has announced protests at more than 1,200 universities over the issue. Its leaders have also questioned the credibility of the state-appointed SIT into the alleged examination irregularities, citing repeated changes in its composition.The protesters have so far refused to call off the agitation, maintaining that they will continue the movement until their demands are addressed.

World.title: UP Creators Summit & Awards to celebrate the state's rising digital voices and creator economy in grand 2-day event
World.content:
As India's creator economy continues to redefine entertainment, entrepreneurship and storytelling, Uttar Pradesh is emerging as one of the country's fastest-growing hubs for digital innovation.

With increasing internet penetration, a thriving startup ecosystem and the rapid rise of creators from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities, the state is playing a pivotal role in shaping India's digital future.

Celebrating this transformation, the inaugural edition Times of Indiaâs UP Creators Summit & Awards will bring together some of the state's most influential content creators, industry leaders, brands and digital innovators for a 2-day mega showcase of recognition, insightful conversations and future-focused learning.

To be held on August 19 and 20 in Varanasi, the spiritual and cultural heart of Uttar Pradesh, the event will bring together the stateâs rich heritage and its new-age digital voices, showcasing how creators are shaping the narrative of a new Uttar Pradesh. The first day, August 19, will feature insightful masterclasses, panel discussions and fireside chats, while August 20 will culminate in the grand UP Creators Awards, celebrating the stateâs most impactful digital creators.





Honouring the creators shaping a new Uttar Pradesh

At the heart of the event are the Creators Awards, which will honour creators who are making a meaningful impact across diverse genres, including education, technology, finance, food, travel, lifestyle, comedy, fashion, gaming, social impact and more. These creators are not only building communities online but are also amplifying local stories, inspiring millions and showcasing Uttar Pradesh's talent on the national and global stage.

The awards celebrate creators who are redefining digital influence while contributing to the state's growing reputation as a powerhouse of innovation and creativity.

Conversations driving the future of the creator economy

Beyond the awards, the summit will serve as a platform for thought-provoking discussions on the opportunities and challenges shaping the creator ecosystem.

Panel discussions will explore how the creator economy is expanding beyond metropolitan cities into Tier 2 and Tier 3 India, the growing influence of creators in rebranding Uttar Pradesh, and the role of digital storytellers in building the narrative of a new Uttar Pradesh.

The event will also feature engaging fireside chats on themes such as "Storytellers of a New Bharat" and "Beyond Followers", examining how creators are moving beyond metrics to create meaningful impact, influence culture and build sustainable careers.

World.title: Parliament Monsoon Session ends amid disruptions; Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha adjourned sine die
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

ended on Thursday with both the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha being adjourned sine die amid repeated disruptions and political confrontations between the government and Opposition.

The session, which began on July 20, witnessed protests inside and outside the Houses over several issues, while Parliament also passed a number of legislations.

Rijiju says session successful in business, but debate fell short

Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said the Monsoon Session was successful in terms of legislative business but fell short on debate and discussion. He said Parliament passed 12 Bills during the session, but productivity remained low amid repeated disruptions.

"In terms of business, it was a very successful session; we passed a total of 12 bills. However, from the perspective of debate and discussion, it was not as successful," Rijiju said.

He said the Lok Sabha recorded 19 per cent productivity against the total time allotted, while productivity in the Rajya Sabha stood at 39 per cent. Rijiju attributed the lower productivity largely to disruptions by Opposition parties, while noting that NDA members and MPs from some Opposition parties participated in debates.





Rijiju said only one Bill in the Lok Sabha â the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, dealing with paper leaks and unfair means in examinations â underwent a full discussion. The legislation was also discussed in the Rajya Sabha.

He criticised the Opposition for not allowing debates to proceed, saying the government was ready to provide answers to questions raised by Opposition MPs. "This is not healthy for the parliamentary democracy," Rijiju said.

He also accused Congress MPs of focusing on slogans, placards and protests instead of parliamentary debate, and said he hoped there would be a change before the Winter Session.

"In the Lok Sabha, 11 bills were passed without discussion, while one underwent discussion," Rijiju said, adding that the concerned Bill was fully discussed in the Rajya Sabha.

Rajya Sabha skips question hour, passes Mines and Minerals Bill

The Rajya Sabha was adjourned sine die after chairman C P Radhakrishnan highlighted the performance of the House during the session.

Deviating from the normal pre-lunch schedule on the final day, the Upper House dispensed with the Zero Hour and Question Hour and took up the Mines and Minerals Amendment Bill. The legislation was subsequently passed by a voice vote.

The Rajya Sabha had witnessed repeated disruptions during the session over issues including police action against students protesting the alleged NEET paper leak and allegations concerning the theft of donations at the Ram temple in Ayodhya.

The House also witnessed a confrontation between leader of opposition Mallikarjun Kharge and the government over an alleged 'Shuddhikaran' or purification ritual at a stage in Haldwani after Kharge addressed a Congress rally there on August 8.

Kharge raised the issue in the Rajya Sabha, saying he had spoken about people's problems and had not mentioned any community or religion during his speech.

âBut after my speech, people associated with the BJP carried out a 'purification' ritual of that stage,â Kharge said, questioning whether such an incident was appropriate in a democracy.

Leader of the House JP Nadda said the BJP did not support such activities and assured the House that the allegation would be investigated.

âWhat Kharge ji has said is truly a matter of concernânot just for the Congress party, but for all of us,â Nadda said. âI want to make it absolutely clear that the BJP does not subscribe to such activities.â

Chairman C P Radhakrishnan said untouchability was condemned by all members and asked the government to investigate the allegation and punish those responsible if it was found to be true.

Lok Sabha ends amid opposition protests

The Lok Sabha was also adjourned sine die soon after proceedings began on the final day, following the traditional playing of Vande Mataram.

Proceedings were disrupted by Opposition MPs amid sloganeering, with political tensions also spilling into the Parliament complex.

BJP and opposition held counter-protests at the Makar Dwar steps, with the BJP protesting against Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi over the Congress' position on the ongoing protests in Jharkhand.

Opposition MPs, meanwhile, raised demands for the Union Home Minister to make a statement in the House and for the Prime Minister to respond to issues raised by them.

Congress MP Imran Pratapgarhi accused the ruling party of preventing Parliament from functioning.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

âIt is the ruling party itself that is preventing Parliament from functioning,â he said, arguing that the Opposition had been seeking discussions and responses from the government on issues including the Public Examinations Amendment Act.

Union minister Manohar Lal Khattar rejected the opposition's allegations and said Parliament could not function without discussion.

âThe Lok Sabha is a forum for discussion. There is no point in proceeding without discussion,â Khattar said. He added that the House was a platform for representatives from across the country and âdoes not belong to any single individualâ.

The session ended after weeks of political confrontation, with disruptions remaining a prominent feature of proceedings in both Houses.

World.title: Messi visit row in Kerala: possible Vigilance inquiry referral hinges on confirmation of involvement of government funds and resultant loss to the exchequer
World.content:
A Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB) inquiry into the previous Left Democratic Front (LDF) government’s failed bid to host the 2022 FIFA World Cup-winning Argentina football team and its iconic captain, Lionel Messi, in Kochi in Kerala in 2025 would hinge on whether the current multi-department inquiry revealed any involvement of government funds resulting in a loss to the exchequer.

Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan had confirmed on Saturday (August 8, 2026) that the Finance department, headed by him, has opened an investigation into suspected GST levy evasion on foreign remittances, amounting to a projected ₹156 crore, purportedly made by the project’s sponsor, a television news broadcasting company, to the Argentine Football Association to secure Messi and his team’s presence in Kochi.

Suspected tax evasion

According to government sources, wilful evasion of GST on foreign remittances liable to tax, if revealed during the inquiry, could constitute a non-bailable felony under the Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) Act, 2017, which entails a punishment of up to five years of imprisonment and a fine. They said the Finance department’s probe would also probably examine whether any government official had aided the suspected service tax evasion.

Notably, Mr. Satheesan had stated that the previous LDF government’s Finance department had flagged the suspected evasion and issued a notice to the sponsor. However, he said, there was, “rather inexplicably,” no further enforcement action.

According to the government sources, the ongoing verification would also examine whether there were any procedural lapses on the part of the Greater Cochin Development Authority (GCDA) in the handing over of the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium at Kaloor in Kochi to the sponsor for renovation ahead of the Argentine football team’s “anticipated” visit.

They said the Sports department report had questioned the sponsoring firm’s claim that it had transferred ₹126 crore to the Argentine Football Association (AFA) as an upfront payment for their arrival, allegedly without any contractual agreement involving cash transfer with the footballing body, a potential offence under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999, if proved.

An official said a FEMA violation need not necessarily trigger an offence under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, unless investigators can prove the alleged contravention was linked to a criminal offence.

The ongoing Finance department verification, sources said, would also examine whether former Sports Minister V. Abdurahiman’s trip to Spain at the sponsor’s behest to meet AFA officials, at ₹13-lakh loss to the State exchequer, ostensibly to give Kerala’s sporting sector a boost by securing the football team’s friendly match in Kerala, violated administrative procedure such as the Chief Minister’s authorisation and mandatory clearance from the Ministry of External Affairs.

The ongoing inquiry may also verify the legality in the previous dispensation’s selection of the sponsor for the event, allegedly without open tendering, financial background checks, and necessary clearances, officials said.

World.title: Jharkhand exam stir: FIR against 300 unnamed people in connection with August 10 march to Assembly
World.content:
Police on Thursday (August 13, 2026) lodged an FIR against 300 unnamed people in connection with the August 10 march to the Jharkhand assembly over alleged recruitment examination irregularities in the state, a senior officer said.

The case was registered against the unnamed people for violating prohibitory orders, causing damage to government property and attacking police personnel, he said.

“An FIR has been lodged against 300 unknown miscreants at the Vidhan Sabha police station for disrupting the peaceful march to the assembly on August 10,” Ranchi SP Paras Rana told PTI.

The process to identify these miscreants is underway through video footage, said SDPO (Hatia) Neeraj Kumar.

The job aspirants have been demonstrating for the past 20 days in Ranchi over the alleged irregularities.

World.title: Akali Dal chief Sukhbir Badal attacked in Maharashtra’s Nanded; one held
World.content:
Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) president Sukhbir Singh Badal suffered a hand injury in an attack by two unidentified persons allegedly wearing the attire of a Nihang, in Maharashtra’s Nanded on Thursday (August 13, 2026).

One of the suspects has been taken into custody and investigation is under way, Nanded Collector Rahul Kardile said. Police said preliminary information suggests that they used a kirpan (dagger) that was with them to carry out the attack.

Mr. Badal, who is on a two-day visit to Nanded district, was visiting various gurudwaras when he was attacked at the Mata Sahib Gurudwara. “He suffered a minor injury on the hand. He is stable and out of danger,” Mr. Kardile said, adding that the police inspector who saved the SAD chief also sustained injuries. Mr. Badal’s wife, Lok Sabha MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal, was also present at the time of the incident.

Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis ordered a probe into the attack, directing the police to investigate motive.

In 2024, Mr. Badal had averted an assassination bid after a former militant and pro-Khalistan sympathiser opened fire at him outside the Golden Temple in Punjab’s Amritsar, where he was performing penance for his ‘mistakes’.

Mr. Badal escaped unhurt in the incident even as the accused was overpowered by security police personnel. He was sitting at the entrance of the Golden Temple, attired in the dress of a ‘sewadar’ performing the penance, when the accused person drew a gun to shoot.

SAD demands high-level probe

Senior SAD leader Daljit Cheema demanded a high-level independent inquiry into the incident.

“Mr. Badal was in Nanded and after paying obeisance at Takht Sachkhand Sri Hazur Abchalnagar Sahib Gurudwara, he had gone to another Gurdwara nearby, when a person in his mid-sixties attacked him with a ‘kirch’ (dagger). The person was wearing traditional attire (bana). What is the actual conspiracy behind the incident, and who is the person? Whether he is actually a Nihang or belongs to some group will only be known after the investigation,” Mr. Cheema told The Hindu.

“This is a serious matter. Whenever Akali Dal rises, conspiracies start right then,” he added.

With PTI inputs

World.title: Naidu opens Seed Access Road second phase, two steel bridges at Amaravati
World.content:
Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Thursday (August 13, 2026) inaugurated the second phase of the Seed Access Road (E-3), along with two steel bridges, at Undavalli, describing the development as the first major step towards building the capital city.

Mr. Naidu unveiled the plaque at Undavalli to mark the inauguration and addressed a public meeting attended by Municipal Administration and Urban Development Minister P. Narayana, Civil Supplies Minister Nadendla Manohar, APCRDA Commissioner V. Vijay Rama Raju, MLAs Tenali Sravan Kumar and Kolikapudi Srinivas, MP Bhashyam Ramakrishna, farmers and residents.

Two steel bridges, 110 and 280 metres, open in Amaravati on Thursday, giving the capital direct road links to Vijayawada and Mangalagiri. Also being handed over: 216 quarters for MLAs and MLCs across nine towers at Nelapadu.



Video: K.V.S. Giri pic.twitter.com/oIqfqs7bVb — The Hindu - Andhra Pradesh (@THAndhra) August 12, 2026

The Seed Access Road has been completed from Rayapudi through Venkatapalem, Penumaka and Undavalli. The project, developed at an estimated cost of ₹1,519 crore, is planned for expansion in its third phase to connect the capital region with National Highway 16 near Manipal. The bridges will improve connectivity between Vijayawada, Mangalagiri and Amaravati.

The two steel bridges are a 110-metre structure across the Buckingham Canal and a 280-metre bridge across the Kondaveeti Vagu and the Guntur Channel. Mr. Naidu walked some distance down the bridges, inspecting the construction.

Addressing the gathering, Mr. Naidu recalled that farmers had contributed about 34,000 acres for the capital, and paid tribute to those who gave their lands. He said the capital’s development had been disrupted during the previous government, forcing the present government to close contracts, retender works and restart construction.

"Even a child can identify the centre of A.P. It is Amaravati," CM Chandrababu Naidu says at the inauguration of the steel bridges and Seed Access Road at Undavalli on Thursday, recalling how land pooling was chosen over acquiring 50 acres for a conventional Secretariat.



📹 TDP pic.twitter.com/iQZMJ2bjt2 — The Hindu - Andhra Pradesh (@THAndhra) August 13, 2026

Mr. Naidu said Singapore had supported the Amaravati master plan and Norman Foster’s London-based firm had been engaged for the iconic government buildings. He rejected criticism that Amaravati was merely a “graphics” project, saying the vision was becoming reality.

He said Amaravati would be developed as a pollution-free deep-tech capital, with AI and quantum-computing hubs, with the aim of placing it among India’s top five cities. He said the capital region would cover Amaravati, Mangalagiri, Tadepalli, Guntur and Vijayawada, and that the Centre had sanctioned a 190-km outer ring road and a 96-km inner ring road.

The project also envisages underground utility corridors for electricity, gas, telephone and water services across Amaravati. Mr. Naidu said Amaravati would be inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2028 as a capital admired by the country. Calling the Seed Access Road and the steel bridges the first step, he urged people to contribute ideas and work towards making Andhra Pradesh a “Swarna Andhra” by 2047.

World.title: Vande Mataram row: Kerala govt’s stance will be ‘made clear’ on Independence Day, says CM Satheesan
World.content:
Amid the Opposition’s allegations that the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) government in Kerala was toeing the Sangh Parivar’s line after the Chief Secretary’s directive to government departments to ensure the recital of ‘Vande Mataram’ in its entirety during the Independence Day celebrations, Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan has said the State government has “its own stand on the issue, which will be clear to everyone on Independence Day”.

Speaking to the media after the Cabinet meeting on Thursday (August 13, 2026), Mr. Satheesan did not explicitly state that Vande Mataram will not be sung in its entirety, though press persons raised questions on the confusion that has arisen due to the Chief Secretary’s directive.

Instructions were reportedly issued in some schools and institutions mandating that the song be sung in full.

“The Chief Secretary’s directions were related to the Union government’s Har Ghar Tiranga campaign. The Parliament has now passed a Bill making intentional insult to Vande Mataram a punishable offence with jail term up to three years. It mandates that the song be sung in full. The President has also given assent to the Act. However, the Congress-led UDF has a clear stand on this. We will act only as per that,” he said.

As per the directive signed by Chief Secretary Bishwanath Sinha on August 6, the Union Ministry of Culture had on July 14, 2026 communicated that the Har Ghar Tiranga campaign will be observed this year from August 9 to 17. The campaign has been integrated with the third phase of the nationwide commemoration of the 150 years of Vande Mataram. Accordingly, all physical celebrations during this period have to combine the collective singing of Vande Mataram with the hoisting of the national flag.

The letter further states that the “instructions of the Government of India for recitation of Vande Mataram will be followed in full”.

The Local Self-Government department and the General Education Department are the nodal departments for the programme. However, an earlier circular issued by the General Administration Department on August 4 does not make any mention of Vande Mataram recital as part of Independence Day celebrations.

Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan had said that singing the first two stanzas of Vande Mataram was not wrong, but the song in its entirety went against the secular spirit of the country, which was the opinion of the Constituent Assembly also. The later stanzas of the song refer to deities of a specific religion.

World.title: Lebanon abolishes death penalty: Where does capital punishment still exist?
World.content:
Lebanon’s parliament on Tuesday (August 11, 2026) voted to abolish the death penalty, making it the first country in the Arab world to replace capital punishment with life imprisonment with aggravated hard labour. The legislation will come into effect after it is signed by the President and published in the Official Gazette.

According to lawmaker Imad al-Hout, who supported the bill, the legislation reduces sentences for people facing the death penalty and life imprisonment to 17 “prison years”. In Lebanon, where a prison year is generally calculated as nine months, this amounts to 12 years and nine months of actual imprisonment.

Lebanon has maintained an unofficial moratorium on executions since January 2004. However, courts have continued to hand down death sentences. At the end of 2025, 85 people were on death row, according to the Lebanese Ministry of Justice’s Directorate of Prisons.

Which countries still retain the death penalty?

According to the latest report by Amnesty International on death sentences and executions, nearly three-quarters of the world’s countries had abolished the death penalty in law or practice as of December 2025. Some countries that have abolished capital punishment in practice have retained it in law but have not carried out executions for at least 10 years.

Some countries have abolished the death penalty only for “ordinary crimes”. This means capital punishment may still be permitted for exceptional offences, such as certain crimes under military law or offences committed in exceptional circumstances.

Executions continue to rise

Despite the global decline in the use of capital punishment, executions increased sharply in 2025. Amnesty International recorded at least 2,707 executions worldwide in 2025, up 78% from 1,518 in 2024.

The increase was driven largely by Iran, where Amnesty recorded at least 2,159 executions in 2025, more than double the 972 executions recorded in 2024.

Amnesty’s figures do not include the executions believed to have been carried out in China, which continues to classify data on executions as a state secret.

World.title: Syama Prasad Mookerjee’s contributions to be included in educational curriculum from 2027: Suvendu
World.content:
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Thursday (August 13, 2026) said the State’s Education department will include in its curriculum chapters on the contributions of freedom fighter Syama Prasad Mookerjee from the next academic year.

The decision was taken at the first meeting of a special committee constituted to plan and implement programmes marking Mookerjee’s 125th birth anniversary.

“The Education Department will include a dedicated section on Syama Prasad Mookerjee in the curriculum from the next academic session. His contributions will be taught at the school and the university level,” Mr. Adhikari said.

The meeting reviewed various aspects of the curriculum and books on Mookerjee along side matters related to to installation of his statue with the objective of highlighting his life, ideals and contributions.

The State government will also publish a book on Mookerjee, as part of the programmes planned to mark his 125th birth anniversary, the Chief Minister said.

World.title: Britain poised for record hot summer as western Europe swelters under another heat wave
World.content:
Large parts of western Europe will be sweltering once again on Thursday (August 13, 2026), with Britain poised for its fifth heat wave of an exceptional summer that is expected to be the hottest on record.

Forecasters are predicting the mercury to rise as high as 38 Celsius (100 Fahrenheit) in central and southeast England, falling just short of the August record of 38.5 C, set in 2003.

The Met Office said earlier this week that only average conditions were needed for the rest of August to beat last year's record for the hottest year.

For a country that's largely not equipped to deal with these levels of heat, it's been a particularly uncomfortable few weeks. Air conditioning is a rarity outside of shops and offices.

Working has been particularly difficult in hospitals, where nurses have been known to collapse from heat exhaustion, according to the Royal College of Nursing.

Also read | Europe’s early heat wave led to rise in deaths, may have killed over 10,000

“When nursing staff are collapsing, feeling dizzy, sick or even being admitted to the very hospitals they work in because their workplaces cannot handle the heat, it shows just how badly they are being failed,” said RCN chief executive and general secretary Professor Nicola Ranger.

The bulk of the country is now officially in drought, heaping pressure on water resources for households, agriculture and the environment to mitigate, all of whom have to look for mitigations both in the short-term and in the long-term in the face of human-caused climate change.

Southern Water, which oversees supplies in the south of England, has applied for a rare drought order which would ban businesses from non-essential water use, including cleaning cars and filling non-domestic swimming pools, saying an “exceptional” lack of rain has threatened supplies in Hampshire and the Isle of Wight.

Environment Secretary Angela Eagle will decide on the application, which would be the first such ban since May 2006.

Meanwhile, wildfires have been blazing uncontrollably, most notably this week in the New Forest in southern England. Some 1,017 wildfires have been recorded in England and Wales this year, according to data from the National Fire Chiefs Council, the same as last year's record-breaking total.

Though not on the level as those witnessed in France, Greece and Spain, they provide ample evidence of the need for the U.K. to adjust to a new reality.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said he will consider imposing a ban on disposable barbecues amid the risk of further wildfires as extreme heat continues to grip parts of the U.K.

“I do believe we need to get the message out loud and clear,” he said. “People should not be using those barbecues outside at this moment in time.”

World.title: 'A service to the world': Norwegian minister praises Pakistan's leadership for US-Iran mediation efforts
World.content:
Norwegian Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide expressed his country’s appreciation of Pakistan’s mediatory role in the ongoing US-Iran conflict on Thursday, saying it was a “service to the world and, hence, also to us”.

Eide, who is on a two-day visit to Pakistan, expressed these views while addressing a press conference alongside Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar in Islamabad.

“I also really want to reiterate our strong support for the very important role that Pakistan has taken in this dramatic war that started on February 28 with the US-Israel attack on Iran,” he said, recalling that Norway was one of the Western countries that was “clearest and earliest” in stating that the war was a violation of international rules.

“If we stand up for international law, it has to apply to everyone, everywhere, all the time,” he stressed.

He said that while Norway had “significant disagreements with Iran on other issues, they also have the right to be protected as a state”.

Coming to Pakistan’s mediatory role in the ongoing conflict, he said he realised how difficult mediation and facilitation of parleys between the two sides could be.

“I know what a massive task you were taking on when you offered Islamabad not only as the venue but also as the facilitator of these talks,” he said, lauding Pakistan’s civilian and military leadership for their efforts.

“What you have been doing is really a service to the world, and hence, also to us.”

The Norwegian foreign minister said Pakistan’s mediation efforts also mattered to his country as it was a large shipping nation.

“We share an interest in open sea lanes and the ability to trade in the high seas, and to respect the Constitution of the Oceans […] Whatever emerges from this tragic and unnecessary war in Gulf, we need to protect the principle of the free passage,” he explained. “And I am so happy we see completely eye to eye [on this],” he remarked.

The visiting minister added that his message to “anyone involved out there in the conflict is that this issue of free passage and an open strait is not an issue for the warring parties alone. It is a global issue that we have a shared interest in promoting”.

He said he had discussed other regional issues during the visit as well, ranging from the Kashmir issue to Afghanistan.

Moreover, Eide said, he was glad to learn more about a recently signed defence pact between Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia in Makkah.

“These are three countries with whom Norway has very good and close relations,” he noted.

At the outset of his address, Eide said he was honoured to be in Pakistan, saying the last time a Norwegian foreign minister visited Pakistan was 10 years ago.

“So it was about time,” he remarked. “I promised you many months ago that I would come, and today, I live up to my promise. I was looking forward to this visit, which is short but very effective.”

Eide said there was a “strong partnership” between Norway and Pakistan, as well as the people of the two countries.

“We have a sizeable diaspora of Pakistani descent […] Many of them are in key positions of politics and society and are a very welcome contribution to our country; and the fact that we have so many people who know these two countries intimately is yet another argument for strengthening our economic ties,” he added.

The Norwegian foreign minister further said that Oslo and Islamabad were discussing strengthening economic ties “in the context of specifics” and enhancing trade ties in more structural ways.

He also mentioned climate change and floods in Pakistan, saying that the two sides agreed it was a foreign policy issue.

“And if you need one additional argument for stopping wars apart from relieving suffering and ending economic harm, it is that mankind should collectively try to focus on the real issues that require real cooperative action,” he said.

Eide mentioned combatting nature loss, climate change, promoting global health and fighting poverty in this connection, adding that all of them were on his agenda for discussions during the visit.

Speaking before him, Dar said the two countries had agreed to enhance their ties and cooperation in all areas of mutual interest, including trade and investment, education, defence, climate change, IT and maritime affairs.

He said Pakistan greatly valued its relations with Norway and looked forward to further strengthening these ties in the days, weeks and months to come.

Moreover, he continued, bilateral political consultations (BPC) between the two countries had become a regular feature. “We are looking forward to hosting the next round of BPC in Islamabad later this year in the winter,” he said.

Dar said the two sides also agreed that bilateral trade between Norway and Pakistan was “below the potential of both economies and needs to be enhanced through effective measures”.

“Pakistan offers enormous investment opportunities to Norwegian companies, and it is heartening to see many leading Norwegian companies investing in Pakistan.

“A renowned Norwegian company, Yara International, is establishing a joint venture in plant nutrition with the Fauji Fertiliser company. I hope this initiative will be a trailblazer for many more future projects between our two great countries,” he added.

Dar termed Pakistan’s partnership with Norway in the field of technology “a success story”.

“Pakistan’s IT exports to Norway have grown more than five-fold in the last two years, and I have no doubt that this is only the beginning.”

He further stated that the two sides also agreed on the expedient finalisation of various agreements and memoranda of understanding (MoU).

On climate change, he said there was a convergence of perspectives between the two countries.

“It is heartening to note that Pakistan and Norway signed the MoU under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement on April 1 this year,” he said, adding that the two sides also held talks on cooperation in maritime affairs.

He said he had told the visiting dignitary that Pakistan was “one of the world’s largest ship recycling facilities, and our strategic location makes it the most competitive and nearest recycling destination in this maritime region for ships coming from Norway”.

Dar thanked Norway’s maritime authorities for their support in capacity building and providing technical training for Pakistan’s shipbreaking industry in line with the Hong Kong International Convention.

He added that Pakistan and Norway had agreed to enhance people-to-people contact, which he said could become “defining for our relations and serve as social and cultural bridges between the two countries”.

The DPM said the two sides had also discussed labour mobility.

“We agreed to continue work on legal pathways for Pakistan’s skilled manpower, expressing the need to combat human smuggling and illegal migration. Both sides agreed that by providing safe, orderly and regular migration channels, we not only protect migrants’ rights and lives but also dismantle the illegal model of smuggling networks,” he elaborated.

Dar further said that both Pakistan and Norway shared a commitment to multilateralism, the principles of the United Nations Charter, respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity and the peaceful settlement of disputes.

“Our two countries remain actively engaged on issues related to the UN Security Council, and the two sides have strong convergence of views on major issues.

“Building on our previous experience of working together in international bodies and multilateral fora, both sides affirm their desire to continue mutual support and consultations on such forums.”

Dar said he had also briefed the Norwegian foreign minister and delegation on the Kashmir issue. He said he told them that India had added a new dimension to an already volatile security situation by unilaterally announcing the abeyance of the Indus Waters Treaty in contravention of international law.

“We reiterate that India must end the weaponisation of water and uphold its treaty obligations under international legal obligations,” he asserted.

Dar said he had further briefed the Norwegian foreign minister on Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts for promoting dialogue, de-escalation and peaceful settlement of the US-Iran conflict. He thanked him for appreciating Pakistan’s role as a mediator in the conflict.

Moreover, he said, he had broadly discussed the Makkah defence pact with the visiting dignitary. “We had a great discussion, and it happens that all three countries enjoy the best of relations with Norway,” he said.

The DPM concluded his address, saying: “We agreed on the need to find peaceful solutions to the international conflicts in full respect of the principles of international law and the UN Charter.

“I thank his excellency, my dear friend, for his visit. I am confident that this visit will open a new chapter in Pakistan-Norway relations and will contribute to greater cooperation and mutual prosperity for the people of both countries in the years ahead.”

Delegation-level talks

Eide had commended Islamabad’s mediation efforts after his arrival in the federal capital earlier in the day as well, and as he held delegation-level talks with Dar, according to the Foreign Office (FO).

The visiting dignitary recognised Pakistan’s role as “important and constructive”, the FO said.

“The Norwegian foreign minister commended Pakistan’s important and constructive role during the recent Iran-US conflict, including the leadership and contributions of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, DPM Dar and Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir,” it said.

Both sides reviewed the whole gamut of bilateral cooperation in various fields, including trade, investment, climate change, maritime affairs and education. They recognised the important role of the Pakistani diaspora in Norway and agreed to strengthen people-to-people ties between the two countries, it added.

The two sides expressed satisfaction at the warm and cordial state of Pakistan-Norway relations and agreed to further deepen cooperation in areas of mutual interest,” it said.

The FO said the two sides also held in-depth discussions on regional and international developments of mutual interest.

In televised remarks, Eide appreciated Pakistan’s efforts to promote peace and expressed Norway’s desire to further strengthen bilateral ties.

He said Norway and Pakistan had a “very strong bilateral partnership”, adding that the presence of a large Pakistani community in Norway, which was “well integrated into Norwegian society”, had helped strengthen ties between the two countries.

“There are many leading politicians in Norway and many close colleagues who are actually of Pakistani-Norwegian descent, so it has really made a mark,” he said.

Eide said business ties between the two countries were also growing, particularly in the energy and fertiliser sectors, with Norwegian companies increasingly looking at opportunities in Pakistan.

He said Norway also saw opportunities for Pakistan to strengthen economic relations through its cooperation with Switzerland and Iceland, noting that the three countries could provide further avenues for expanding business relations.

Turning to the regional situation, Eide strongly commended the actions taken by Pakistan’s leadership, including the prime minister and foreign minister, in efforts to promote peace in the Middle East.

Eide described the ongoing war as “incredibly dangerous” for global peace as well as the world economy, and praised Pakistan for stepping forward. He also appreciated Pakistan’s role in facilitating the Islamabad talks and maintaining engagement with the parties involved.

“I think it is fair to say that the position of Pakistan on the world stage, also in peacemaking, has really been strengthened by this commitment,” he said.

Eide said Norway was ready to assist Pakistan’s peace efforts, noting that Oslo had experience in peace negotiations and maintained open dialogue with both Tehran and Washington.

“Wherever we can be useful, we will,” he said.

He also highlighted Norway’s experience in international maritime affairs, saying the country was among the world’s major seafaring nations despite its relatively small population.

He said Norway could therefore play a constructive role in discussions concerning international maritime law and developments surrounding the Strait of Hormuz.

Dar, Eide discuss bilateral ties

Earlier, the two ministers held a “restricted-format meeting”.

“DPM Dar warmly welcomed Eide to Pakistan. The two ministers discussed the full range of bilateral relations, as well as regional and international developments, and reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening bilateral cooperation in all areas of mutual interest,” it said.

Upon his arrival in Islamabad, Eide was received at the airport by Additional Foreign Secretary (Europe) Ambassador Ayesha Ali.

In a statement on Wednesday, the FO said the minister is undertaking the visit from Aug 13-14 at Dar’s invitation.

The visit is the first by a Norwegian foreign minister in a decade, the FO said, adding that the visit would build on high-level engagement between the two countries, including phone conversation between Dar and Eide in March and April, and the visit of Norway’s State Secretary Andreas Motzfeldt Kravik to Islamabad in May.

The FO stated that the visit would provide an opportunity to “further strengthen the longstanding and cordial relations between Pakistan and Norway and to explore new areas of mutually beneficial cooperation”.

World.title: Pakistan, Turkiye, Saudi Arabia will form political, military mechanisms to coordinate under defence pact, Ankara says
World.content:
Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia will form political and military mechanisms under a defence pact signed between the regional powers last week, Turkiye’s defence ministry said on Thursday, adding the alliance would also deepen defence industry cooperation.

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement was signed last week as the Middle East grapples with fallout from the US-Israeli war on Iran , which has dragged in regional players and disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea.

At a weekly briefing in Ankara, the ministry said the mechanisms would include the three countries’ defence ministers, foreign ministers, and military chiefs.

It added that the joint military exercises were also being planned under the pact, while cooperation could include joint production and technology sharing in the defence industry.

The remarks come a day after Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said that he hoped more countries would join the agreement.

“Our vision for it is not limited to the three countries,” the Turkish leader told the London-based Asharq Al-Awsat daily.

“Rather, we aspire for it to grow, and perhaps appropriate conditions will emerge one day for all countries of the region to gather under its umbrella.”

Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan on Saturday said Turkiye expected Egypt to join the pact “in the next stage”, telling the Anadolu state news agency only “a few technical issues” stood in the way.

Egypt has not commented on the agreement nor on the remarks by Fidan, who will visit Cairo on Thursday and Friday.

Kuwait , Bahrain and Somalia are among the countries that have welcomed it. Iran’s comments also took a rather positive tone, stressing its stance of pursuing “security mechanisms based on cooperation between regional countries”.

World.title: AJK police claim JAAC 'abducted' 8 highway police personnel on election duty
World.content:
Azad Jammu Kashmir (AJK) police said on Thursday that eight highway police personnel on election duty had been “abducted” by the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC).

Addressing a televised press conference, police spokesperson Khawar Ali Shaukat alleged that the JAAC attacked security forces deputed on election duty in the region.

“Eight highway police officials on election duty were abducted,” he said as state media shared a collage of the officials’ pictures.

“The personnel are in the custody of JAAC and have been subjected to brutal abuse,” he said. He said that the “miscreants also threatened the families of the personnel that they would be martyred if their demands were not met”.

He said that recent events showed that the JAAC was not a peaceful group, but a violent one intent on challenging the state’s writ and weakening institutions.

“I want to make it clear that the state was not and is not weak. The state has always shown restraint,” he said, adding that violent acts for the sake of rights were not above the law.

He said that the people of the region, by participating in polls in the region, had made it clear that they had nothing to do with the proscribed group. He appealed to the public to disassociate themselves from the JAAC and to not get involved in acts where the state’s writ was challenged.

He appealed to parents to keep an eye on their children, saying: ““They play with the future of young people and instigate them against state through misleading propaganda and provocative statements.”

At the end of his press conference, he called on the JAAC to free the abducted personnel.

“The state will not accept any pressure with regards to the lives of these officials. If the personnel are harmed, obstacles are created in their release or threats to their families continue, the state will not show any leniency,” he said.

“If the state’s writ is challenged and if state officials are subjected to violence … the state will carry out its duties in accordance with the law and the Constitution,” he said, vowing strict action against such elements.

“Any group that challenges the state’s writ will be dealt with accordingly,” he said.

The JAAC, which has been demanding the abolishment of 12 seats in the local legislature reserved for refugees from Indian-held Kashmir, has been holding protests in the region for several weeks now.

Clashes took place between protesters and law enforcement personnel in Rawalakot and Mirpur on July 28, which reportedly resulted in several casualties. Amid the tensions, elections are being held across the region in phases.

The government has accused militant elements “pursuing a foreign agenda and backed by Indian funding” of fomenting the unrest.

Last week, AJK Information Secretary Muhammad Rashid Hanif said that seven law enforcement personnel, including those from police and Rangers, were martyred during recent unrest in the region.

World.title: Body of missing Pakistani climber Sohail Sakhi recovered on Broad Peak
World.content:
The body of Pakistani climber Sohail Sakhi, who was among the 10-person expedition that went missing after the deadly Broad Peak avalanche, was recovered and shifted to the mountain’s base camp, the Alpine Club of Pakistan (ACP) said on Thursday.

The avalanche struck on July 30, cutting off contact with the 10-member international expedition led by world-renowned British-Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja on Broad Peak, one of the world’s highest mountains. Purja’s company later confirmed there were no survivors .

The bodies of seven climbers were found. However, the search for Sakhi, American climber Sarah Mallory Geis, and Nepalese climber Nawang Thindu Sherpa was suspended last week due to a risk of fresh avalanches.

On Thursday, ACP member Naila Kiani said that Sakhi’s body had been found. According to Naila, a team of local volunteers from Shigar, searching the area on their own initiative, found the remains, which were subsequently confirmed as those of Sakhi.

She said the volunteers — Muhammad Nadeem, Muhammad Bashir and Abuzar — first spotted the body and alerted others in the area. They, along with other volunteers, brought the body down from Camp 1 to the base camp.

ACP General Secretary Ayaz Shigri told Dawn that the body had been shifted to the Broad Peak Base Camp and would be airlifted to Skardu by Pakistan Army helicopters, weather permitting.

He said the bodies of two remaining climbers have not yet been recovered. Shigri said rescue efforts for the remaining climbers would resume once weather conditions improved and the area was deemed safe.

He said the local volunteers located Sakhi’s body at an altitude of 5,600 metres.

Renowned mountaineer Nirmal Purja along with six elite Nepali guides were also part of the expedition. Purja, who served with Britain’s Brigade of Gurkhas before joining the Special Boat Squadron of the Royal Marines, had broken multiple climbing records since becoming a full-time mountaineer and tour guide.

World.title: SHC orders formation of committee to probe HIV outbreak among children at Karachi hospital
World.content:
KARACHI: The Sindh High Court (SHC) directed the provincial government on Thursday to constitute a committee for an “independent, impartial and comprehensive” inquiry into the HIV outbreak among children at Karachi’s Kulsum Bai Valika Hospital.

A two-member SHC bench, headed by Justice Adnanul Karim Memon and comprising Justice Muhammad Jaffer Raza, issued the directive as it announced its reserved judgement on a plea seeking an independent inquiry, registration of a case and lifelong medical treatment as well as appropriate compensation for the affected children.

The outbreak was initially reported late last year, following which the Sindh government carried out screening at the Sindh Employees Social Security Institution (SESSI)-run hospital located in Karachi’s SITE area. According to data shared by the Sindh government, at least 78 children have been found infected with HIV at the hospital while a screening in the nearby area also confirmed 120 additional cases.

But Advocate Tariq Mansoor, the lawyer who moved the SHC on the matter, claimed in his petition filed in May that the total number of infected children is around 200.

The court observed in its order on the plea that the departmental proceedings and reports submitted so far had been “insufficient to determine the number of affected persons, the source and circumstances of transmission, compliance with infection-control protocols and the Sindh Regulation and Control of Disposable Syringes Act, 2010, as well as the supervisory and individual responsibility of the officials concerned”.

Keeping this in view, the court deemed it necessary “in the interest of justice, transparency and public confidence that an independent fact-finding mechanism be constituted by the competent authority, without expressing any final opinion regarding the guilt or innocence of any individual”.

It directed that a committee, headed by the Sindh chief secretary, be constituted. The chief secretary should co-opt two senior officers not below the rank of BS-20 and “preferably having no direct administrative involvement in the affairs of the hospital or the proceedings under inquiry” to join the committee, the court order stated.

The court directed that the committee should determine:

The actual number and particulars of children and other patients who were found HIV-positive and who received treatment at the hospital during the relevant period

The source, circumstances and possible mode of transmission of HIV, based on available medical and scientific evidence

Whether any disposable syringe or other medical equipment was reused, improperly disposed of, inadequately sterilised or otherwise used in violation of the applicable law, rules, protocols or standard medical practice

The existence and implementation of infection-prevention and control protocols at the hospital

The procurement, supply, storage, distribution and use of auto-lock, auto-destruct or auto-break syringes and the relevant record

The role and responsibility of medical, nursing, technical, administrative and supervisory officials concerned

Whether any officer or official, by act or omission, failed to discharge a statutory, administrative or supervisory duty

The status and legality of the departmental proceedings already initiated against the 37 officials and whether such proceedings adequately address the actual responsibility of the persons concerned

Whether any provision of the Sindh Regulation and Control of Disposable Syringes Act, 2010, or any other applicable law has been violated and, if so, the persons responsible

The measures required for preventing recurrence of any such incident in the future

The court order further stated that the committee should be empowered to examine all relevant records, including medical and laboratory reports, screening data, procurement and stock registers, syringe records, duty rosters, infection-control and inspection reports, inquiry proceedings, CCTV footage where such incidents occurred in Sindh and other material necessary for an “objective determination, while affording a fair opportunity of hearing to any person against whom an adverse finding is proposed”.

The committee should submit its comprehensive report to the competent authority, as well as the SHC, within two months of its constitution, the order read. It elaborated that the report should identify “the factual position and, where supported by evidence, fixing responsibility and recommending appropriate departmental, statutory or criminal action pursuant to Section 7 of the Sindh Regulation and Control of Disposable Syringes Act, 2010”.

Pending the inquiry, the Sindh chief secretary should ensure through the relevant departments and SESSI that all affected HIV-positive children and other identified patients receive “comprehensive, uninterrupted and appropriate medical treatment”, including medicines, investigations, counselling and follow-up care, entirely free of cost, at any institution of higher standard as medically appropriate, the court ruled.

“All such expenses shall be borne by the government/SESSI and shall not be recovered from the affected patients or their families, and the arrangement shall continue for as long as medically required,” the court directed.

Noting the “extraordinary circumstances of the case and the vulnerability of the affected children”, the court further directed the provincial chief secretary to determine and process the “entitlement of each affected child/ family to compensation, financial assistance or other lawful relief, strictly in accordance with the applicable statutory framework and government policy”.

The chief secretary should ensure that the process is completed expeditiously and without unnecessary hardship to the affected families, the order said.

Moreover, the relevant authorities should ensure that no affected child or family is discriminated against, stigmatised or denied medical, social or other lawful assistance on account of HIV status, the court ruled, adding that the identity and medical information of affected children should be dealt with strictly in accordance with applicable law and accepted medical standards relating to confidentiality.

The court further directed the chief secretary and the health department secretary to ensure immediate preventive and corrective measures at Kulsum Bai Valika Hospital to eliminate any further avoidable risk to patients and strict compliance with the Sindh Regulation and Control of Disposable Syringes Act, 2010, infection-prevention protocols and other applicable health regulations.

Where necessary, they should also ensure the framing of requisite rules in accordance with law, the court order added.

The court also observed that the matter concerned the protection of the rights to life, health, dignity and fair treatment and warranted an independent, transparent and evidence-based inquiry.

“The matter cannot be treated merely as an administrative issue, as the constitutional obligation to protect life under Article 9 [of the Constitution] extends to ensuring effective discharge of public-health and medical-safety responsibilities, particularly towards vulnerable patients,” the court order read.

However, it added, “allegations or departmental proceedings cannot by themselves establish individual culpability, which must be determined based on evidence and after due opportunity of hearing”.

Show-cause issued to petitioner

The court order also stated that during a hearing, the petitioner, Advocate Mansoor, “raised his voice and instigated the private persons accompanying him, prima facie to attract the media and allowed the private persons to record videos in court, which is a contemptuous act on their part”.

The act, the court observed, disrupted proceedings and “seriously disturbed the decorum and dignity of the court”.

“The unruly conduct of the petitioner and the persons in the shape of a mob present in court compelled this court to retire to chambers to complete the order, although almost the entire order had already been dictated in open court.

“Prima facie, the petitioner, being dissatisfied with the conclusion of the matter, attempted to obstruct the court from proceeding further in accordance with law,” the order read.

It added that the incident also exposed a “serious security lapse” on the part of the in-charge of court security, including the relevant deputy superintendent of police and senior superintendent of police.

They were also called upon to explain their position, and they sought time to hold an inquiry.

“Prima facie, they are directly responsible for maintaining order and security within the court premises. Their apparent negligence and failure to discharge their duties enabled a mob brought by the petitioner for his convenience to enter the courtroom, indulge in hooliganism and flagrantly disregard the authority and decorum of this court. Such conduct amounts to an unacceptable interference with the administration of justice, for which the petitioner and the persons acting with him must be held responsible in accordance with law,” the order read.

Therefore, the court directed that Mansoor be issued a show-cause notice, seeking an explanation as to why criminal and contempt of court proceedings may not be initiated against him.

The order stated that the petitioner should submit his written reply before the next date of hearing in separate contempt proceedings, either personally or through counsel, and to continue appearing in person on each date unless such appearance is dispensed with by this court.

“The representatives of the Sindh High Court Bar Association (SHCBA) and the Sindh Bar Council (SBC) were also called upon to intervene in the matter, who also sought time to call upon the petitioner for such misconduct and are also directed to be in attendance in the proceedings,” the order said, adding that the court office should place this matter before the SHC chief justice.

The bench also directed the SHCBA and SBC to take immediate and appropriate remedial measures in accordance with law, including coercive measures against the apparent misconduct of the petitioner.

Meanwhile, court security officials should identify the private persons involved in the incident and initiate appropriate proceedings against all those responsible, the bench directed.

It further instructed the court registrar to preserve and secure the CCTV/ video recordings of the areas inside and outside the courtroom so that the persons involved may be identified and appropriate action may be taken strictly in accordance with law to “secure and preserve the dignity of the court”.

World.title: Water-starved citizens ‘squeezed’ further for more Karachi Water and Sewerage Corporation revenue
World.content:
KARACHI: While the Karachi Water and Sewerage Corporation (KWSC) is widely blamed for failing to provide water in many areas connected to its piped network across the metropolis, the utility has burdened Karachi residents with higher costs as it notified a uniform 7.05 per cent increase in water and sewerage charges for its residential and bulk consumers.

The latest increase has marked the second major hike in just two years as in September 2024 the corporation had increased its monthly charges by roughly 23 per cent.

At the time, sewerage charges were set at nine per cent of water charges.

The decision draws widespread criticism from the public who have to rely on water tankers as the KWSC failed to ensure uninterrupted water supply in their areas.

Uniform 7.05pc increase in monthly water and sewerage charges notified

A notification published in the Sindh Government Gazette on August 10, 2026 made the increase official, following approval by the KWSC Board of Directors to revise both retail and bulk tariffs in line with the average Consumer Price Index.

Under the revised tariff, monthly water and sewerage charges for residential plots will be based on plot size, while fixed monthly rates have also been set for various categories of commercial establishments and shops.

The hike in water and sewerage charges triggered concern and anger among people, many terming it injustice to people who did not even get adequate water supply despite paying hefty bills.

Muhammad Irfan, a resident of Gulshan-i-Iqbal, said that they got water only twice a month and that too for hardly half an hour. “We still have to buy tankers and now we have to pay the full increased bill. Where is the justice in this?“ he asked.

A housewife from Model Colony, Sadia Butt, said that after electricity and gas, now the water had gone up too.

“With a seven per cent increase, everyone’s bill goes up,” she said adding that it was already so hard to manage expenses these days.

Abdul Ghafoor, a shopkeeper in Khokrapar, Malir, said that there had been no piped water in his area at all, still the water utility sent them a fixed bill without meters. “With this fresh hike, small traders like us will face more burden,” he added.

A resident of Saddar said: “The government says it will provide facilities. We don’t get facilities, instead the bill increases every year.”

KWSC officials said that the objective of the revision was to strengthen the corporation’s revenue base and generate sustainable resources for water supply and for the operation, maintenance and rehabilitation of the city’s sewerage network and other civic services.

According to KWSC data, the corporation collected Rs8.14 billion in the first four months of 2026, with average monthly revenue now exceeding Rs2.26 billion.

However, the KWSC’s recovery rate remains low as in FY24 only 36 per cent of billed grievances were resolved within the stipulated time under the previous system in financial year 2024-25.

The KWSC Act 2023 provides the legal cover for such revisions, empowering the utility to adjust tariffs annually in accordance with inflation without seeking fresh legislation each year.

The KWSC officials said that without additional revenue, service delivery would deteriorate further and the revision was also tied to the utility’s commitments under the World Bank-funded Karachi Water and Sewerage Services Improvement Project.

Published in Dawn, August 13th, 2026

World.title: Gas supply to parts of Balochistan suspended after main pipeline blown up in Bolan
World.content:
QUETTA: The gas supply to several towns and cities of Balochistan, including parts of the provincial capital, was suspended late on Wednesday after a main gas pipeline in Bolan area of Kachhi district was blown up by unidentified miscreants.

The Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC) confirmed the incident and said that the 18-inch wide gas pipeline was badly damaged, disrupting the supply.

A statement by its spokesperson said that the explosion occurred at the KMP-246 Valve Assembly in the Bolan riverbed area near Gorkat, around 700 to 800 metres from the main Quetta-Sibi Road.

It said that unknown people planted explosives under the pipeline in the riverbed and detonated it with a remote control.

The company said the gas supply was suspended to Kolpur, Mach, Mastung, Kalat, Pishin, Ziarat and many parts of Quetta and added that consumers may face reduced gas pressure or supply.

Local sources said unidentified individuals allegedly targeted the main valve of the gas pipeline with explosives in the Daraz Bent area of Bolan. Following the explosion, flames and smoke were seen rising from the damaged pipeline.

SSGC said that teams were ready to initiate repair work, but they were waiting for security clearance before going to the affected area. The gas utility said its management was closely monitoring the situation and working to restore supplies as soon as possible.

In May, the gas supply to a vast area of the province was suspended after unknown armed men blew up a gas pipeline in the Dera Bugti area. The same month, the supply to Sohbatpur district in the Nasirabad division was also suspended after unidentified miscreants blew up a gas pipeline.

A similar incident also occurred in March as unidentified armed men blew up the main gas pipeline at Western Bypass area.

World.title: US senators demand inquiry into conditions aboard aircraft carrier deployed in Middle East
World.content:
Congressional Democrats demanded answers on Wednesday about conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, following reports of food shortages, broken plumbing and mental health crises during the aircraft carrier’s record-setting deployment.

In a letter to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth Wednesday, Senator Richard Blumenthal called for the Navy to account for conditions aboard the aircraft carrier, which “has been deployed more than 250 days” without coming ashore “in over 200 days, setting a record for consecutive days at sea.”

Blumenthal voiced concern for such extended deployments, noting “widespread reports of shortages of basic supplies, water contamination, plumbing issues, deteriorating mental health, deck safety concerns” and other problems aboard the Lincoln.

Senator Ruben Gallego called for “an official oversight visit with the bipartisan Senate Delegation to the USS Lincoln to investigate the reported alarming conditions,” in a post on X.

The USS Abraham Lincoln departed San Diego, California on November 21, 2025 for duty in the South China Sea and was rerouted to the Middle East before US-Israeli attacks on Iran that began February 28.

In two recent meetings, family members clashed with Navy leadership over the difficult conditions — including food shortages — faced by the 5,000 sailors and Marines aboard the Lincoln and demanded to know when loved ones would return home, MSNOW reported.

Some reported severe mental health issues and attempted suicides on board.

“The stories of crew members threatening to jump off the ship are a frightening alarm bell as to how bad the situation has become: moldy showers, sporadic hot water, rationed meals and soap, broken toilets, and grueling 12- to 16-hour shifts with no days off,” Gallego wrote in his post on Wednesday, adding that he has served in active duty himself.

“The way (US President Donald Trump) is treating our service members as he carries out this illegal war is not just disgusting, it’s dangerous.”

The US Navy did not immediately respond to an AFP request for comment.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni

The impact is already visible. In the readymade garments sector, gas shortages and load shedding are reducing productivity by 25–30 percent in many cases. This threatens export earnings, foreign currency reserves, and economic stability. The crisis has also reached ordinary households. Although Bangladesh declared 100 percent electrification in 2022, many rural areas still experience 10 to 20 hours of load shedding every day during summer. This affects education, small businesses, agriculture, and people’s dignity.

We have also seen long lines at fuel stations, schools moving online, and offices shortening working hours because of fuel shortages. These are not isolated events. They show how deeply energy insecurity can disturb national life.

Over the last 15 years, electricity tariffs in Bangladesh have been increased on many occasions, including more than 10 rounds of increases at both bulk and retail levels. This path is not sustainable. Fossil-fuel-based electricity depends on imported fuel, global prices, the availability of the dollar, subsidies, and repeated tariff adjustments. Solar power offers a different path. With a one-time investment, solar can provide stable energy for 15–20 years. Once installed, its fuel cost is almost zero.

The economic comparison is clear. A 1 MW HFO-based power plant produces electricity per year at a cost of nearly BDT 190 crore, with much of the cost paid in foreign currency. In contrast, a 5 MW solar project requires a one-time investment of around BDT 25 crore, after which fuel costs are practically zero. Each 1 MW of solar power can save around USD 325,000 per year in foreign currency.

This is why renewable energy should not be discussed solely in technical terms like decarbonisation, emissions, and sustainability. For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Despite Bangladesh’s potential, renewable energy contributes less than 5 percent to power generation, far below the global 30 percent target by 2030. Clear, measurable goals and timelines are essential for effective policy planning and investment decisions.

Renewable energy equipment imports face around 50–60 percent in duties and taxes, hindering local manufacturing growth. Policy reforms that reduce import duties and support local industry can accelerate renewable deployment and reduce dependency on imports.

For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Import duty is usually imposed to protect the local industry. But where local production is not yet significant, a high duty only increases project costs, reduces investment returns, and slows renewable energy expansion. Policy reforms can unlock this potential, making stakeholders feel their efforts directly contribute to progress.

India, Pakistan, Vietnam, and China have expanded solar and wind power by offering low or zero import duties, tax exemptions, and low-interest financing. Many countries have also reduced duties on lithium-ion batteries and energy storage systems. Bangladesh should learn from these examples.
